## Story

The strongest story in this data is not about one country or one year. It is about a broad pattern that repeats across many observations: people in countries with stronger economies tend to live longer, and the gap between low-income and high-income countries narrows as development proceeds.

This is exactly the kind of pattern we can test with real-world data. We are not relying on a fixed opinion or a training plan; we are observing how variables move together in the world itself.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px

df = pd.read_csv('data/gapminderDataFiveYear.csv')
latest = df[df['year'] == 2007].sort_values('gdpPercap', ascending=False).head(10)

fig = px.bar(
    latest,
    x='gdpPercap',
    y='country',
    color='continent',
    orientation='h',
    title='Top countries by GDP per capita in 2007',
    labels={
        'gdpPercap': 'GDP per capita (USD)',
        'country': 'Country',
        'continent': 'Continent'
    },
    hover_name='country'
)

fig.update_layout(
    template='plotly_white',
    width=1100,
    height=500,
    legend_title='Continent',
    title_x=0.5
)

fig.show()
```

### Key takeaways

- The dataset shows a consistent relationship between income and health outcomes.
- The trend is strongest when viewed across many countries and multiple years.
- By 2007, the high-income countries sit at both the top of GDP per capita and the top of life expectancy.
- This kind of project is useful because it gives us a real answer rather than a static recommendation.

The project is now grounded in an actual observational data set, and the homepage and analysis tabs work together to make the evidence readable and explainable.
